svg.title: A nurse in an emergency department is caring for an 8-year-old who is up to date with current immunization recommendations and has a deep puncture injury. Which of the following should the nurse anticipate administering?
svg.desc: Td is the wound-prophylaxis product from the 7th birthday onward , and it is the 10-year booster after 18. This child is 8 and up to date, so a Td booster is all that is anticipated. DTaP is the childhood formulation for children under 7 and is not used for wound prophylaxis. Tdap is for completing the pertussis series or as the one-time adolescent dose (licensed from age 10, and used for catch-up at 7–10) — not for wound prophylaxis. TIG mixed with DT is wrong twice: TIG is for someone not up to date with a dirty or deep wound, and TIG and a toxoid are never drawn into one syringe — separate syringes, different sites.
